summary.text: Tara Hong is a Democratic state representative from the 18th Middlesex District who has served in the Massachusetts House of Representatives since January 2025 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
Hong emigrated from Cambodia to Lowell in 2013 and graduated from UMass Lowell before working for Lowell nonprofits and the university.

paragraphs.text: Tara Hong emigrated from Cambodia to Lowell, Massachusetts, in 2013 with his mother and sister.
He attended Lowell High School, Middlesex Community College and UMass Lowell, where he earned a bachelor's degree in political science with a minor in criminal justice.
Hong served on the board of Mill City Grows from 2021 to 2024 and on the board of the Cambodian Mutual Assistance Association from 2023 to 2024.

He worked as a program assistant at UMass Lowell's Asian American Center for Excellence & Engagement, as a program coordinator at Project LEARN, and as a civic engagement coordinator at the Cambodian Mutual Assistance Association.
Hong took office on January 1, 2025, succeeding Rady Mom.
He serves on the Joint Committees on Community Development and Small Businesses, Election Laws, Environment and Natural Resources, and Higher Education.

In a Ballotpedia survey, Hong named constituent services, education and affordable housing as key messages of his campaign and said he is also passionate about food security, economic opportunity, and supporting immigrants, seniors, veterans and working families.
